title: Several repositories
summary: A roster of your repositories, a note channel between them, one supervisor repository that speaks for you, and a shared kit kept in sync.
why: With several repositories on one machine, a finding in one is often a problem in all of them. A channel and a supervisor let you fix it once, without pasting the same instruction into every session.

items.title: Roster of your repositories
items.does: Creates ops/roster.json: one entry per repository with its code, name, root (entered in the wizard), colour, and whether it is retired.
items.why: Every report kept its own list of repositories, and the lists disagreed; one roster read by all of them settles it.
items.notes: Keep the file gitignored in a public repository: it holds your local paths.

items.title: Note channel between repositories
items.does: Adds the channel rule (outbox first, byte-copy delivery, re-hashed destinations, an N/M count) and an outbox README.
items.why: Without a channel, each repository re-diagnosed the same machine finding on its own, and triage by title missed the section that mattered.

items.title: Supervisor notes count as your instruction
items.does: Adds the rule that a hash-verified note from the supervisor repository is your instruction, bounded by the floors.
items.why: It gives you one place to act across all repositories instead of pasting the same order into each session.

items.title: Cheap inbox triage
items.does: Copies kit_inbox.py and adds the inbox cost rules: free classification first, mechanical acknowledgements, a daily outbound cap and a hop limit.
items.why: When measured, about 60 percent of background spend was repositories chatting about notes rather than doing work.

items.title: Kit files are pinned copies
items.does: Adds the rule that kit files are byte copies pinned by their manifest, and copies the manifest that pins them.
items.why: Local edits to shared helpers forked them silently; a pinned manifest makes any fork visible.

items.title: Managed shared rules block
items.does: Adds the rule that the shared rules in CLAUDE.md are rendered from the enabled modules and changed only through the profile, which reports a hand edit.
items.why: One rule text for every repository only stays one text if nobody edits a copy.

items.title: Drift check every session
items.does: Adds the start-up step that runs the profile status check for every repository in the roster.
items.why: A fork caught at the next session start is a one-line fix; caught a month later it is an archaeology project.

items.title: At most one kit version a week
items.does: Adds the rule: one new profile version per seven days, built on a worktree branch, the next only after all repositories adopted the last; fixes exempt.
items.why: Repositories stopped their own work to adopt version after version; a slower train let them build again.

items.title: Watcher helper
items.does: Copies kit_watch.py: a watcher primitive that takes a baseline first, advances only after delivery, runs once at a time and reports going stale once.
items.why: Hand-written watchers re-delivered old history or died silently; one primitive does it correctly.

items.title: Agent applies OS settings itself
items.does: Adds the grant that firewall, network adapter, service and UAC changes are made by the agent instead of being handed to you to paste.
items.why: The author prefers the agent to make such changes with backup and read-back than to type them by hand. This hands real power to the agent, so it stays off unless you choose it.

items.title: Nightly note delivery and drift record
items.does: Registers a nightly task (04:00, 55-minute limit) that delivers queued notes to every repository and records each one's profile drift; it applies nothing.
items.why: Delivering kit notes during the day made repositories stop mid-session to adopt; once a night they do it while idle.
